strings.name: Rihanna
strings.role: Singer and creative entrepreneur · Music, beauty and fashion
strings.summary: Rihanna moved from Barbados into the US recording industry, combining Caribbean rhythms with pop, R&B and dance music. From Music of the Sun through Good Girl Gone Bad to ANTI, she developed her sound through changing collaborations and visual styles. She later expanded into beauty, fashion and philanthropy; Fenty Beauty’s range of foundation shades helped prompt wider discussion of representation in cosmetics.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to the May 2025 song release. Reports of recording a later album are not treated as a completed or released album.
strings.influence.rationale: Built international influence through music, performance and beauty ventures, bringing Caribbean culture and representation of diverse skin tones into the mainstream.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: A changing musical language
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: From “Umbrella” to ANTI, developed a distinctive recording and performance style across pop, R&B and Caribbean music.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Broadening representation in beauty
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Launched Fenty Beauty in 2017 with foundations covering a wide range of skin tones.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Releases “Friend of Mine”
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Released a song for the animated film Smurfs, continuing her work with cinema and soundtracks.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Headlines the Super Bowl halftime show
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Performed a selection of hits in Arizona, presenting her catalogue with suspended platforms and an ensemble of dancers.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Records a song for Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Released “Lift Me Up,” contributing to the film’s musical remembrance and receiving a Grammy nomination.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Named a National Hero of Barbados
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Received the national honor during celebrations marking Barbados’s transition to a republic.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Launches Fenty Beauty
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Launched the cosmetics brand with collaborators, offering 40 foundation shades and emphasizing a broad range of skin tones.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases ANTI
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Released her eighth studio album, developing a looser, stylistically varied sound in songs including “Work.”
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Founds the Clara Lionel Foundation
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Established a foundation named for her grandparents to support education, health and community projects.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Wins her first Grammy
strings.timeline.event-08.text: “Umbrella,” featuring Jay-Z, won Best Rap/Sung Collaboration, marking a major milestone in her international career.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases Good Girl Gone Bad
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Changed her musical and visual approach with songs including “Umbrella,” expanding her place in international pop.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Releases her debut album
strings.timeline.event-10.text: After signing with Def Jam, released Music of the Sun, introducing Caribbean rhythms to international listeners through “Pon de Replay.”
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Barbados
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Saint Michael and raised in Barbados; began singing as a teenager before entering the recording industry.
